title: Elephant Encounter Turns Tragic for Tourists Near Mount Cameroon
excerpt: A Swiss hiker died and British and American visitors were hurt after a sudden elephant herd crossed their trail in Cameroon’s Mount Cameroon National Park.
body:
## A Day That Took a Dangerous Turn
A group of six adventurous travelers set out for a hike near the village of Bakingili, on the southern edge of Mount Cameroon National Park, on 19 November. The party included four British tourists, one Swiss visitor and an American, all guided by local experts. The path they chose is a well‑known route that elephants use to reach a nearby lake.

## The Unexpected Herd
While navigating the trail, the hikers suddenly found themselves face‑to‑face with a herd of roughly fifteen elephants. The massive animals, moving together, caused panic among the group. In the chaos, the Swiss tourist, Alain Throo – an insurance executive based in London – was gored. He later succumbed to his injuries. The British and American members of the party also sustained injuries, though details on their condition were not disclosed.

## Safety Concerns in Wildlife Areas
The incident highlights the risks of trekking in regions where wildlife corridors intersect popular hiking routes. Local guides often warn visitors to stay alert, especially during the dry season when animals travel farther for water. While the guide team acted quickly, the suddenness of the encounter proved deadly for Throo and left the others wounded.

The story was reported by The Guardian, underscoring the need for heightened safety measures and better signage in areas where tourists and wildlife share the same paths.
